question: Will the U.S. and Argentina have signed a new 123 civil nuclear cooperation agreement as of September 10, 2026?

factors.description: No bilateral event on the calendar in the Aug 19 – Sep 10 window. Milei's confirmed 2026 US itinerary (reported Aug 9, 2026) is UNGA New York in late September (~Sep 22-26), Washington on October 14 for a Hispanic Heritage Month conference, and the G20 in Miami in December — FM Quirno accompanies on the latter two. The IAEA General Conference is also late September. Every natural signing venue falls AFTER the resolution date.

Argentine government's own framing (Aug 10, 2026, unnamed Casa Rosada sources) is 'coordinating with Washington the diplomatic aspects to arrange the signing during the coming months' with a target of 'before the end of the year' — plural months, not weeks. No date, venue, or ceremony has been announced by State, DOE, or the Cancillería.

Very low deadline pressure. The 1997 agreement runs to Oct 16, 2027. Even allowing for the post-signature presidential determination plus 90 days of continuous congressional session, signing anytime through roughly mid-2027 still permits entry into force before expiry. Nothing forces action in the next three weeks.

Resolution criteria are narrow and exclude several plausible near-term news events. Fine print bars a mere extension of the 1997 agreement. An MOU/NCMOU (the Paraguay template), initialing of text, or a joint statement announcing 'negotiations concluded' would all still resolve NO. Only an actual signature by authorized representatives counts.

Substantive negotiating work is done: Casa Rosada sources say the technical drafting was finalized (text fully articulated at the Feb 25-27, 2026 JSCNEC meeting in Washington) and only diplomatic scheduling remains. This removes the usual multi-month tail of textual haggling and means a ceremony could be arranged on short notice.

Trump-administration civil-nuclear momentum, including in Latin America: US–Saudi 123 agreement signed July 22, 2026 (Sec. Wright + Prince Abdulaziz at DOE); US–Paraguay civil-nuclear MOU signed Aug 4, 2026 (Rubio + FM Ramírez Lezcano at the State Dept). Both were minister-level ceremonies requiring no summit, and such ceremonies are typically announced only days in advance — so absence of an announcement today is weaker evidence than it would be for a leaders-level event.

summary:
Status quo is NO and the window is only 22 days. Verified independently: no signing has occurred, and the most recent reporting (Aug 10, 2026, unnamed Casa Rosada sources, replicated across several Argentine outlets) says the technical text is finalized but the Cancillería is still "coordinating with Washington the diplomatic aspects to arrange the signing during the coming months," targeting "before the end of the year." No date, venue, or ceremony has been announced by State, DOE, or the Cancillería.

The calendar is the dominant consideration. Milei's confirmed 2026 US itinerary (reported Aug 9) is UNGA in late September, Washington on October 14, and the G20 in Miami in December — FM Quirno accompanies on the latter two. The IAEA General Conference is also late September. Every natural signing occasion falls after the September 10 resolution date, and there is nothing on the books before it. Deadline pressure is minimal: the 1997 agreement runs to October 16, 2027, and even with the post-signature presidential determination plus 90 days of continuous congressional session, signing as late as mid-2027 still permits entry into force before expiry.

I modeled the signing date as a hazard process over Aug 19 – Dec 31, mixing three hazard shapes (uniform 35%, event-clustered 45%, back-loaded toward year-end 20%) with P(signed by year-end) ~ Beta(5.8, 4.2), mean 0.58. Result: 5.2%, stable in a 3–7% band across reasonable variants; the grid corners run 1.9% to 14.0%.

The genuine case for a higher number is that the US–Saudi 123 (signed July 22, 2026 at DOE) and the US–Paraguay civil-nuclear MOU (August 4, 2026 at State) were both minister-level ceremonies with no summit attached, announced only days ahead — so "nothing announced today" is weaker evidence than it looks, and the text being finished means the residual barrier is purely scheduling. That is why I do not go below 3%. But the criteria are strict: an extension, an MOU on the Paraguay template, initialing, or a "negotiations concluded" statement all resolve NO, and those are the more likely near-term outputs of a warming relationship. I settle at 5%, slightly above the factor sum (3.6% off my 9.5% anchor) to leave room for the short-notice-ceremony channel.
reasoning:
**Forecast: 5%** — the U.S. and Argentina are unlikely to have signed a new 123 agreement by September 10, 2026.

## Key findings

**Status quo is NO, and the window is only 22 days.** I verified independently that no signing has occurred — the most recent relevant reporting is August 10, 2026.

**The Argentine government's own timeline points past the deadline.** Wire copy sourced to unnamed Casa Rosada officials (replicated across ANRoca, NoticiasNet, El Cordillerano, Diario Panorama, cholilaonline) says the technical text was finalized at the February 2026 JSCNEC meeting, but the Cancillería is still "coordinating with Washington the diplomatic aspects to arrange the signing **during the coming months**," targeting "before the end of the year." No date, venue, or ceremony announced.

**Every natural signing occasion falls after September 10.** Milei's confirmed 2026 U.S. itinerary (reported Aug 9): UNGA in late September, Washington on October 14, G20 Miami in December — FM Quirno accompanies on the latter two. The IAEA General Conference is also late September. Nothing is on the books before the resolution date.

**Deadline pressure is minimal.** The 1997 agreement runs to October 16, 2027. Even with the presidential determination plus 90 days of continuous congressional session, signing as late as mid-2027 still allows entry into force before expiry.

## Method

I modeled the signing date as a hazard process over Aug 19 – Dec 31, mixing three hazard shapes (uniform 35%, event-clustered 45%, back-loaded 20%) with P(signed by year-end) ~ Beta(5.8, 4.2), mean 0.58. Result: **5.2%**, stable in a 3–7% band; grid corners run 1.9% to 14.0%.

## The strongest counterargument

The U.S.–Saudi 123 (July 22, 2026, at DOE) and U.S.–Paraguay civil-nuclear MOU (August 4, 2026, at State) were both minister-level ceremonies with no summit attached, announced only days ahead. That weakens the calendar argument and is why I don't go below 3%. Cutting the other way: the criteria are strict — an extension, an MOU on the Paraguay template, or a "negotiations concluded" statement all resolve NO, and those are the likelier near-term outputs.
